newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ export growth suggests NZD not overvalued-Birch.
newsitem.headline: NZ export growth suggests NZD not overvalued-Birch.

text.p: New Zealand Finance Minister Bill Birch, speaking to Reuters Financial Television in Hong Kong and monitored in Wellington, said on Wednesday that export growth over 1996 suggested that the New Zealand dollar was not overvalued.
Birch said some exporters had been under pressure from low commodity prices.
"What I think one should recognise is that, even during this period, say right through calendar '96, our export volumes have steadily moved up.
"We have seen a 10 percent growth of export volumes across the export sector. That is not an indication of an overvalued exchange rate," Birch said.
Birch said New Zealand interest rate differentials with the rest of the world were now much narrower than previously.

He repeated comments that the Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash had largely achieved his aim of a lower exchange rate and higher interest rates. Birch said he could understand Brash's concern about the monetary policy mix.
"To some extent we have seen that rebalancing over the last month," Birch said, adding that 90-day bank bills had recently risen.
"He (Brash) has really achieved that rebalancing within his monetary policy settings," Birch said.
Birch was in Hong Kong as part of an investment tour that had taken him through New York and London.
